title: Medusa and Eagle Speculative Decoding: Multi-Head Tree Verification for 3x Faster LLM Inference
summary: Autoregressive generation in large language models is fundamentally memory-bound, spending 95% of its wall-clock time transferring gigabytes of neural weights across GPU memory buses to predict a single token. Classic speculative decoding pairs a small draft model with a large target model, but maintaining two distinct models complicates production deployment and creates distribution shift. Modern architectures like Medusa and Eagle solve this by attaching multiple lightweight prediction heads directly to the base model and generating tree-structured candidate tokens verified simultaneously in a single forward pass.
analogyTitle: The Real-Life Analogy: The Single Executive vs. The Executive with a Predictive Tree Scribe
analogy:
Imagine a CEO dictating a legal contract word-by-word to an assistant.

Under Standard Autoregressive Decoding (Word-by-Word Approval), the CEO reads word #1, pauses 2 seconds to sign off, reads word #2, pauses 2 seconds, and continues. Even for predictable boilerplates like 'in accordance with applicable law', the CEO spends 2 full seconds per word.

Under Medusa Tree Speculative Decoding (The Predictive Tree Scribe), a junior clerk sitting next to the CEO listens to the context and drafts a branching tree of the next four likely words: 'with applicable law' (Branch A) and 'with state regulations' (Branch B). In a single glance taking just 2 seconds, the CEO inspects both branches, approves all 4 words on Branch A at once, and discards Branch B. Four words are finalized in the time it used to take for one.

sections.heading: 1. The Memory Bandwidth Trap of Single-Token Decoding
sections.content:
During the decoding phase of LLMs, every generated token requires loading every parameter in the model from High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) into on-chip SRAM registers. For a 70B FP16 model, that represents 140 GB of memory transfer per token.

• Arithmetic Intensity Crisis: Modern GPUs (like H100s) can perform 1,000 to 2,000 TFLOPS of compute, but their memory bandwidth is capped at 3.35 TB/s. Autoregressive decoding utilizes less than 3% of the GPU's raw matrix compute capacity.
• The Speculative Decoding Opportunity: Processing N tokens in parallel takes virtually the same GPU wall-clock time as processing 1 token, because the model weights are loaded into SRAM once and reused across all N token positions.

sections.heading: 2. Medusa and Eagle: Moving Beyond Dual-Model Drafting
sections.content:
Early speculative decoding required training, hosting, and coordinating a secondary small model (e.g., Llama-3-8B drafting for Llama-3-70B). Medusa and Eagle streamline this into a single unified architecture:

• Medusa Multi-Head Drafting: Adds k lightweight feed-forward heads on top of the base model's final hidden state. Head 1 predicts token t+1, Head 2 predicts t+2, and Head k predicts t+k.
• Eagle: Feature-Level Recurrent Drafting: Rather than predicting tokens from scratch, Eagle passes top-layer hidden representations back into a single lightweight decoder layer, capturing rich semantic context and increasing draft acceptance rates beyond 80%.
• Tree-Structured Attention Verification: Instead of a linear sequence of candidate tokens, the system constructs a candidate tree (e.g., top-3 candidates for step 1, each branching into top-2 for step 2). Using custom 2D attention masks, the base model evaluates all 16 candidate paths in a single forward pass, accepting the longest valid prefix.

sections.heading: 3. Production Serving Integration in vLLM and SGLang
sections.content:
Deploying tree speculative decoding in production serving engines yields immediate throughput multipliers:

• 2.5x to 3.5x Wall-Clock Speedup: On reasoning and coding tasks with high predictability, the target model accepts an average of 3 to 4 tokens per forward pass without altering the model's output distribution.
• Mathematically Lossless Sampling: Through modified rejection sampling, speculative decoding guarantees that the generated text matches the exact probability distribution of the base model, preserving 100% of reasoning accuracy and nuanced voice.

takeaway: Autoregressive generation leaves GPU tensor cores idling while waiting for memory bandwidth. Medusa and Eagle attach lightweight predictive heads to generate candidate token trees, which the base model verifies in a single forward pass, delivering 3x faster inference without altering the output probability distribution.
